side.name: Unemployment
side.line: I can't find work.

side.name: Layoffs
side.line: I could lose my job any day.

why.detail: Someone out of work and someone afraid of losing work are in different places and need different help. Unemployment is having no job now; Layoffs is having one and fearing you'll lose it.

side.name: AI job losses
side.line: I worry AI will replace people's jobs and no one has a plan for them.

why.detail: One is a personal situation today and the other is a societal worry, so people won't confuse them. Unemployment is my own search for work; AI job losses is a worry about what happens to everyone's jobs.

side.name: Underpaid
side.line: I'm paid less than my work is worth.

side.name: Broke
side.line: I run out of money before my next paycheck.

why.detail: Plenty of people are underpaid without running out of money, and plenty run short for reasons other than pay. Underpaid is about pay that doesn't match the work; Broke is running out of money, which can happen for many reasons.

current.name: Underpaid
current.line: I'm paid less than my work is worth.

proposed.name: Broke
proposed.line: I run out of money before my next paycheck.

side.name: Mistreated at work
side.line: My boss or coworkers treat me badly, and I dread going in.

side.name: Burnout
side.line: Work has worn me down so much that I dread every morning.

why.detail: You can burn out under a kind boss and be mistreated without being exhausted, so the two are easy to tell apart. Mistreatment is how people at work treat me; Burnout is being worn down by the work itself.

current.name: Mistreated at work
current.line: My boss or coworkers treat me badly, and I dread going in.

proposed.name: Burnout
proposed.line: Work has worn me down so much that I dread every morning.

side.name: Mistreated at work
side.line: My boss or coworkers treat me badly, and I dread going in.

side.name: Underpaid
side.line: I'm paid less than my work is worth.

why.detail: Low pay and bad treatment often come together, but a person can easily say which one they mean. Mistreatment is about how I'm treated; Underpaid is about what I'm paid.

current.name: Mistreated at work
current.line: My boss or coworkers treat me badly, and I dread going in.

proposed.name: Underpaid
proposed.line: I'm paid less than my work is worth.

side.name: Pointless work
side.line: I spend my days on work that doesn't help anyone.

side.name: Wrong career
side.line: I'm in the wrong line of work, and I don't know how to switch.

why.detail: Someone can be in the right field doing pointless tasks, or in the wrong field doing useful work, and the sharper lines in the alternatives make that choice easy. Meaning is feeling the job doesn't help anyone; Career is being in a field that doesn't fit me and wanting to switch.

proposed.name: Wrong career
proposed.line: I'm in the wrong line of work, and I don't know how to switch.

side.name: Wrong career
side.line: I'm in the wrong line of work, and I don't know how to switch.

side.name: Direction
side.line: I know what I want but not how to get there.

why.detail: Direction covers goals well beyond work, while Career is specifically about being in the wrong job. Career is about the work I do now; Direction is not knowing how to reach a goal I already have, in any part of life.

current.name: Wrong career
current.line: I'm in the wrong line of work, and I don't know how to switch.

proposed.name: Direction
proposed.line: I know what I want but not how to get there.

side.name: Energy
side.line: I'm tired all the time.

why.detail: Tiredness has many causes besides work, and burnout is about the job as much as the body. Burnout is being worn down by work; Tired is being tired all the time, often from sleep or health.

why.detail: Someone can have free hours and still never do anything just for fun, which the first No fun alternative makes explicit. No fun is about play and enjoyment being gone; Busy is about having no time at all.
